items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Has Perrier the music changed in your auction during the last thirty years?

ctx.x: Well, most of the brass bands, they play a watching tempo to walk, and like people are, when you're playing a brass band, you play maybe a six-eighth or two-fourth tempo, like some people call it split time, but it's two-fourth or six-eighth. Four-fourth, too. Yeah, they call it four-fourth, but they play it in two-fourth time. If they play a number, four-fourth number, they're going to play it in two-fourth time, but instead of saying two-fourth, they call it split time. That's what they call it, but it end up…
Has Perrier the music changed in your auction during the last thirty years?

Yeah, yeah, yes, it did a little, because they had better bass drum players years ago. It looked like the bass drum players was different. In fact, they had more of them, and more brass bands. That's the biggest reason for them to chant that, like Inez Rapana and Lil Jim and then the Black Van and them were rough bass drum players, you know. Because you've got some good bass drum players now, but I mean you can count them out on one hand. Count them out on one hand. See, because you've got to play a few marches,…
